boundary: Planning and traceability package only; no certification, accreditation, conformity, safety approval, hardware compatibility, or regulator acceptance is claimed.

requirements.statement: All modeled transfers reject invalid ranges, capacities, overflow, and malformed requests deterministically.
Each adapter exposes explicit start, reset, stop, and monotonic-time behavior with defined error status.
A product hardware identity, revision, firmware, and interface dossier must be independently sourced before hardware claims.
Certification-relevant evidence must be reproducible, hashed, reviewed independently, and linked to requirements and test results.
Every family in the maximum-coverage contract has a deterministic AyeAM behavioral realization and an implementation-independent conformance exercise.
Every contracted family exposes the standalone HAL lifecycle, deterministic logical time, fault injection, reset, and family-specific exercise contract.
Every canonical category sample and every named contract subtype has a unique inventory identity and independent conformance exercise.
Each declared OS target has an explicit binding and QEMU applicability status; emulation evidence is not treated as physical or certification evidence.

processAssumptions.statement: Every released source, toolchain, input, binary, and evidence file is versioned and hash-recorded.
Independence, competence, conflict-of-interest, and review authority are defined before approval decisions.
Accreditation is required only where the applicable scheme, customer, regulator, or contract requires it; scope must cover the exact activity.
